policy.trend_tests: No gap filling. Trend tests use value_clean: months flagged missing, partial_month or low_coverage are left out. Filling would raise the autocorrelation and lower the variance, which makes tests optimistic.
policy.data_mining: Filled on the anomaly, only for the complete month table that mining needs: gaps of up to max_linear_gap_months consecutive months are linearly interpolated; longer gaps get anomaly 0 (the monthly climatology); nothing is extrapolated before the first or after the last usable month. The previous month is never carried forward. Every filled value keeps a fill_method. A series with more than max_fill_fraction of its months filled is not used.
policy.raw_values: value_raw is never changed; flags only mark, they do not delete.

max_fill_fraction.note_en: A series whose filled share of months (between its first and last usable month) exceeds this is not used for data mining (same as trends.py --max-missing-fraction).

max_linear_gap_months.note_en: Gaps of at most this many consecutive months are filled by linear interpolation of the anomaly; longer gaps are filled with anomaly 0 (the monthly climatology). No extrapolation before the first or after the last usable month.

min_coverage.note_en: Months with coverage below this are flagged low_coverage and not used (same threshold as trends.py --min-coverage).

outlier_z.note_en: A month is flagged outlier_suspect when the robust z-score of its deseasonalised anomaly, 0.6745 * (anomaly - median) / MAD, exceeds this in absolute value. Flag only; the value is kept.

MERRA-2 variances (var_*). A trend reflects sampling or algorithm changes, not a physical quantity.
OMI observation geometry (solar and viewing zenith angle). A trend reflects sampling changes, not a physical quantity.

From 2024-07 to 2025-06 GLDAS evapotranspiration is higher than FLDAS (about +0.08 to +0.20 mm/day through 2025-05, +0.04 in 2025-06), in the same months in which the GLDAS shortwave forcing is 15 to 32 W m-2 higher than FLDAS.

The 2001-2026 global land trend has the opposite sign in GLDAS (-0.43) and FLDAS (+0.16 kg m-2 per decade); the two series correlate at 0.08. With one comparison product it cannot be told which is closer to the truth. No clear step was found.
Step of about +0.4 K in the global land mean against MERRA-2 (GLDAS minus MERRA-2, 6 months before and after: +0.43 K); the month matches the NCEP GSI/GFS upgrade of 2011-05-09.
Step of about +0.6 K in the global land mean against MERRA-2 (+0.62 K); the month matches the NEMS GFS upgrade of 2017-07-19.
Step of about -0.6 K in the global land mean against MERRA-2 (-0.66 K); the month matches the FV3-based GFS v15.1 of 2019-06-12.

data_kinds.note: in_situ: measured on site; satellite_retrieval: retrieved from satellite measurements; model: computed by a model or reanalysis. Rules and their basis are in data/seed/data_kinds.json.

gldas_tair.note_en: GLDAS_NOAH025_M.2.1 Tair_f_inst: a forcing input of the GLDAS model run, taken from the NOAA GDAS atmospheric analysis; not an output of the land-surface model and not a station measurement (docs/data/gldas-tair-check.md).
